hero.title: CloudStudioUpload, publish, share, and review point clouds in one place.
hero.subtitle: A browser-ready platform for point clouds, scanner projects, and 3DGS scenes.
hero.webNote: The homepage stays focused on day-to-day publishing work. For heavy production runs or customer rollout, deploy CloudStudio on your own server and manage assets under your own data policy.
hero.sideTitle: A practical publish flow for point clouds and 3DGS.
hero.sideText: Keep the homepage operational: upload source data, watch conversion state, and open the published scene without leaving the platform.
hero.step1Text: Send LAS, scanner ZIPs, pre-converted octrees, or Gaussian PLY files.
hero.step2Text: Convert or register assets so teams can open them instantly in the web viewer.
hero.step3Text: Open the final scene, validate status, and hand over a shareable viewing path.

features.label: Capabilities
features.title: A complete professional toolchain
features.subtitle: From ingest to analysis to export — every step engineered for survey workflows.

measure.title: Precision Measurement
measure.desc: Distance, height, area, angle, and coordinate point measurements. Supports custom CRS and global unit switching with real-time floating results.

volume.title: Volume Calculation
volume.desc: Polygon selection + 2.5D grid integration algorithm, intelligent gap handling, auto-recommended parameters, cut/fill visualization.

clip.title: Clipping & Deletion
clip.desc: Box clip, polygon delete regions, cross-section profile analysis. Supports multi-layer deletion and backend synchronized export.

crs.title: Coordinate System Conversion
crs.desc: Built-in WGS84, UTM, Web Mercator. Supports custom EPSG/PROJ/WKT, and importing .prj/.gsb/.tif parameter files.

vis.title: Multi-Mode Visualization
vis.desc: RGB, elevation, intensity, classification, LOD coloring. EDL eye-dome lighting, X-Ray transparency mode.

profile.title: Profile Triangle Measurement
profile.desc: Direct triangle measurement inside section views. Supports background switching with real-time annotations.

export.title: LAS Export
export.desc: True coordinate rewrite export preserving CRS metadata. Supports backend deletion region synchronization for honest data.

slam.title: SLAM Scanner Support
slam.desc: Automatically discovers and manages scanner projects, recognizes geo_info.csv coordinate files, one-click full-site data and trajectory loading.

adv.label: Why CloudStudio
adv.title: Built for real project delivery.
adv.subtitle: A browser-first 3D delivery platform for survey, construction, and inspection teams that need reliable review, stable performance, and clear customer handoff.

card1.title: From capture to handoff, with less back-and-forth.
card1.desc: Upload source data, review browser-ready scenes, and hand over a clear viewing path in one workflow. Fewer moving files, fewer status gaps, and smoother coordination between field teams and stakeholders.

card2.title: Large scenes stay steady.
card2.desc: A floating-origin pipeline avoids the precision limits that make many WebGL viewers drift. Measurements, overlays, and clipping stay stable even across very large coordinate ranges.

card3.title: Open the scene with a single link.
card3.desc: Clients, managers, and reviewers can open scenes in a modern browser without installing special software. Everyone sees the same view, which makes feedback and approval faster.

scanner.crsBrowserSupportNote: This coordinate workflow supports local coordinates, WGS84, Web Mercator, UTM/UPS, and offline authority-code lookup for common CRS definitions. Parameter files can be imported as `.prj / .wkt / .txt / .json / .csv`. Grid resources can be attached from `.gsb / .gtx / .tif / .tiff`, while `.ggf / .grd` may require conversion to a PROJ-compatible grid before they can be used. Horizontal grids can participate in interactive coordinate display when the current transform chain supports them; vertical geoid and more generic grids are applied mainly through the native PROJ/pyproj transform and export pipeline.

metrics.measuredFillNote: Dominant material below the base surface. Cut and Fill remain shown separately.
metrics.measuredCutNote: Dominant material above the base surface. Cut and Fill remain shown separately.

interpretation.stockpile: {{scenario}}: compares the analysis surface against {{base}}, which is typically interpolated from the selected boundary heights for stockpile-style work.
interpretation.planeCutFill: {{scenario}}: compares the analysis surface against {{base}}. Positive cut means material sits above the fixed elevation; positive net means more fill than cut.
interpretation.groundLocalCsf: {{scenario}}: no reliable class-2 ground support was available, so the base surface was built from a local CSF ground classification inside the selected region. This is usually stronger than the low-percentile fallback, but still review warnings when the selected area contains little visible ground.
interpretation.groundQuantileFallback: {{scenario}}: no class-2 ground support was available, so the base surface was approximated from the low-percentile terrain envelope of the unclassified point cloud. Treat the result as an estimate and review the warnings.
interpretation.groundBoundaryFallback: {{scenario}}: ground support was too weak for a real terrain fit, so the job fell back to boundary interpolation. Inspect the warnings before trusting this result.
interpretation.groundLowSupport: {{scenario}}: compares against a fitted terrain-like base, but the ground support ratio is low. Verify classification quality before relying on the fitted base.
interpretation.groundFit: {{scenario}}: compares the analysis surface against a fitted terrain-like base. Use this when a pile sits on uneven land and you do not want to assume a flat floor.

phrases.The browser edition supports WGS84, Web: The browser edition supports WGS84, Web Mercator, UTM/UPS, and an offline authority-code bootstrap for common countries and regions. Parameter files support `.prj / .wkt / .txt / .json / .csv`. Grid support is backed by native PROJ/pyproj on the server and can import `.gsb / .gtx / .ggf / .grd / .tif / .tiff`. In-browser real-time transforms currently focus on `.gsb` and compatible GeoTIFF horizontal grids; vertical geoid/height grids and more general grids run through native PROJ on the backend.
phrases.How to handle empty grid cells with no s: How to handle empty grid cells with no surface scan points in the selected area
phrases.How to handle empty grid cells with no p: How to handle empty grid cells with no point data. Skip excludes them and lowers coverage. Reference elevation fills with the reference plane and contributes zero volume. Neighbor interpolation estimates height from surrounding known points, useful for occluded or sparse scan gaps.
phrases.DTM mode requires classified ground poin: DTM mode requires classified ground points (Class 2); otherwise it falls back to DSM automatically.
phrases.XYZ values in geo_info.csv are interpret: XYZ values in geo_info.csv are interpreted using the source geographic CRS / ellipsoid selected here. WGS84 is used by default and changes only when you edit it.
